name: Quetiapine

tolerance.full: within a week of continuous use

toxicities: Common label-reported effects include somnolence, dizziness, dry mouth, constipation, weight gain, and postural hypotension.

Serious label warnings include neuroleptic malignant syndrome, tardive dyskinesia, severe hyperglycemia, agranulocytosis, seizures, and QT prolongation reported after overdose or with additional risk factors.
Somnolence, postural hypotension, and motor or sensory instability can lead to falls, fractures, or other injury; abrupt discontinuation may cause withdrawal symptoms.
summary: An atypical antipsychotic medication under the brand name Seroquel. Also used to treat insomnia and mood swings. This drug is very sedating and can stop/slow down psychedelic drug trips. Infrequently abused.
metabolism: Extensively metabolized in the liver, chiefly through CYP3A4. Products include active norquetiapine and inactive sulfoxide metabolites; drug-related material is eliminated in urine and feces.
generalRisks: The label warns of increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis and suicidality monitoring in younger patients treated for depression. Other serious risks include neuroleptic malignant syndrome, potentially irreversible tardive dyskinesia, hyperglycemia/diabetes, dyslipidemia and weight gain, hypotension/syncope/falls, leukopenia/neutropenia/agranulocytosis, seizures, QT prolongation in overdose or susceptible patients, anticholinergic effects, and withdrawal symptoms after abrupt cessation.
saferUse: Use only as prescribed and discuss gradual tapering with the prescriber; abrupt discontinuation can cause withdrawal symptoms.
Somnolence may impair judgment and driving and can contribute to falls. Avoid driving or hazardous machinery until effects are known; take extra care during dose titration.

Follow label-recommended clinical monitoring for weight, glucose and lipids; report fever or signs of infection, severe muscle stiffness with fever or confusion, fainting, or abnormal involuntary movements promptly.
Avoid overheating and dehydration, which can impair temperature regulation; review medicines that prolong QT or add anticholinergic effects with a clinician.
